To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We introduce EXTASEMs, a novel approach for learning lexical taxonomies from textual definitions, and (2) We release six domain-specific taxonomies for the use and evaluation of the community.

(1) We present the first approach for automatically learning lexical taxonomies from definitions; (2) We introduce a novel graph induction procedure for constructing weighted taxonomies; (3) Our approach achieves state-of-the art performance in all taxonomy evaluation experiments; (4) Our approach outperforms previous approaches in all experiments; (5) We provide a large number of taxonomies for six different domains.

we introduce EXTASEM, a novel approach for automatic lexical taxonomy construction, which achieves state-of-theart results in the three main evaluation experiments, and we release weighted taxonomies in six domains for the community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we automatically build lexical taxonomies from large corpora? How can we evaluate them? What are their applications in the NLP community?

the following questions: (1) How to automatically extract taxonomic knowledge from domain terminologies? (2) How to automatically assess the quality of the taxonomies extracted? (3) How to exploit the extracted taxonomies in downstream tasks such as text categorization and semantic role labeling?

the following three main aspects: (a) The extraction of (hyponym,hypenym) pairs from definitions, (b) The automatic induction of taxonomies, and finally (c) The automatic evaluation of taxonomic quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is a very promising approach for the automatic acquisition of domain taxonomies.
the results are good enough for a wide range of applications, but there is still a significant amount of work to be done in terms of quality and coverage.
EXTASEM! is a very good approach to learn lexical taxonomies, and it is also the first to learn weighted taxonomies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method for the automatic construction of domain taxonomies which is based on a novel combination of semantic network, CRF-based algorithms and graph theory.
we propose a new method for the automatic learning and evaluation of taxonomies, which can be applied to any given domain and which achieves state-of-theart results in all the experiments.
we are able to learn a taxonomy from a single definition for a given word.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the automatic extraction of lexical taxonomies can benefit from the use of large-scale, domain-independent semantic networks, such as DBpedia, and that this is a viable alternative to the use of manually-annotated corpora.
, in the context of lexical taxonomization, a very large amount of in-domain data is a more valuable resource than a large number of gold standard examples.

, by exploiting large semantic networks and a CRF-based extraction method, we can automatically build lexical taxonomies which outperform previous methods and are of comparable quality to gold standard ones.
